prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There isn’t a single universal “best” — the best contractor for you will be a Miami‑based, Florida‑licensed roofer with proven experience installing Miami‑Dade/HVHZ‑approved systems, strong local references, proper insurance, manufacturer certifications, and a clear workmanship warranty. If you want, I can pull a short vetted list for your ZIP code; otherwise use the checklist below when choosing.

How to find the best hurricane-rated roofer in Miami
- Verify licenses and approvals
  - Florida DBPR contractor license (search at myfloridalicense.com).  
  - Miami‑Dade County Notice of Acceptance (NOA) familiarity — they must install products and systems that meet Miami‑Dade Product Control or FBC HVHZ requirements.  
  - Manufacturer certifications (GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred, CertainTeed Select, etc.) indicate training and access to extended warranties.

- Check insurance and local presence
  - Ask for General Liability and Workers’ Comp certificates naming you as additional insured during work.  
  - Confirm a local office and permanent address (watch for “storm‑chasers”).

- Look at track record and reviews
  - Read Google, BBB, and Yelp reviews; ask for at least 3 local references for similar hurricane‑rating work.  
  - Request photos of recent Miami installations and permit records.

- Technical capabilities you should require
  - Systems approved for the HVHZ (wind speeds and attachment methods to match your roof’s wind‑uplift design).  
  - Proper deck attachment, hurricane straps/ties where required, correct fastener type and pattern, code‑compliant flashing and secondary water barrier.  
  - Impact‑rated materials if desired (Class 4 shingles) or properly installed interlocking tile/standing seam metal for best wind performance.  
  - Willingness to pull permits and coordinate inspections.

- Warranties and documentation
  - Written contract with clear scope, timeline, payment schedule, and change‑order terms.  
  - Manufacturer warranty documentation and a written workmanship warranty from the contractor (length and transferability).  
  - Proof they will obtain permits and provide final inspection sign‑off.

Questions to ask every bidder
- Are you licensed in Florida and registered with Miami‑Dade? Can you provide license/insurance now?
- Have you installed roof systems with Miami‑Dade NOAs in the last 12 months? Can I see examples?
- Which product/system and wind‑uplift rating will you install? Will it meet HVHZ requirements for my address?
- Will you do a full tear‑off or overlay? How do you handle decking damage found during the job?
- What manufacturer/contractor warranties do I get? Are they transferable?
- Who gets the permit and handles inspections? How will you protect my property?
- Can you provide three local references and a copy of a recent final inspection record?

Red flags
- No local address or refusals to provide license/insurance up front.  
- Pressure for large deposit or “work now, paperwork later.”  
- Vague contract terms, no warranties in writing, or offers that seem “too cheap” for HVHZ‑rated installation.

Typical materials that perform well in Miami hurricanes
- Properly installed standing‑seam metal roofs (high wind ratings).  
- Interlocking concrete/clam shell tiles with proper fasteners and straps (if installed to NOA specs).  
- Impact‑resistant architectural shingles, but only when installed with HVHZ attachment and a secondary water barrier.

Next step
If you want, tell me your ZIP code (or address neighborhood) and I’ll find 3–5 Miami roofing contractors that meet the above checks (licenses, local reviews, manufacturer certs) so you can contact them for bids.
